title: 太…了: too, so
summary: Lets you say something is too much or react strongly, as in 太贵了 and 太好了！
explanation:
太 + adjective + 了 means 'too …' (太贵了 'too expensive') or, with good things, 'so …!' (太好了！'Great!'). The 了 at the end is part of the pattern; the sentence sounds unfinished without it.

不太 + adjective is a gentle 'not very': 不太好 'not so good'. It needs no 了.

examples.en: This piece of clothing is too expensive.

mistakes.why: 太 + adjective is normally closed with 了.
不太 ('not very') doesn't take 了.

why: 吗 would make it a question.
的 doesn't close the 太 pattern.
Correct: 太 before the adjective, 了 at the end.
了 goes after the adjective, not before it.
Use 太 or 很, not both.
Correct: 不太 + adjective, with no 了.
太不冷 isn't how 'not very cold' is said; use 不太冷.

不太小 means 'not very small' and has no 了.
